subject: maths
title: Midpoints, lengths and shapes on the Cartesian plane

scenes.heading: Midpoints, lengths and shapes
scenes.say: Two friends want to meet exactly halfway. If you know where they live as coordinates, you can find the spot in seconds. Today: midpoints, lengths, and areas of shapes on the Cartesian plane.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Meet a friend halfway: half the distance east–west and north–south
scenes.science: Midpoint = average of the x's, average of the y's
scenes.breaks: Real streets bend. A segment on the plane is perfectly straight, so averaging always lands exactly on it.
scenes.say: To meet a friend halfway, you each walk half the distance east to west, and half the distance north to south. That is just averaging your positions. The analogy breaks down because real streets bend, but a segment on the plane is perfectly straight, so averaging always lands exactly on it.

scenes.heading: The midpoint is the mean point
scenes.say: First the segment from A, negative four, three, to B, six, negative five. Average the x values: negative four plus six is two, halved is one. Average the y values: three plus negative five is negative two, halved is negative one. So the midpoint is one, negative one.
scenes.caption: Average the x values: (−4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 1. Average the y values: (3 + (−5)) ÷ 2 = −1. So M = (1, −1).

scenes.heading: Finding a missing endpoint
scenes.question: M(2, −1) is the midpoint of A(−3, 4) and B. Find B.
scenes.say: To find a missing end, take the same step again. From A to M is five right and five down. Do it once more from M, and you land on B at seven, negative six.
scenes.caption: Take the same step again. From A to M is 5 right and 5 down. Do it once more from M, and you land on B at (7, −6).

scenes.heading: Area of a triangle from coordinates
scenes.say: Here the base P Q is horizontal, from negative three to five, so it is eight long. The dashed height goes from R down to the base: from four down to negative two is six. Area is eight times six, halved: twenty-four square units.
scenes.caption: Base PQ = 8. Height = 6. Area = 8 × 6 ÷ 2 = 24 square units.

scenes.heading: Box it, then chop the corners
scenes.say: This triangle has no flat side. So draw a box around it: six by six, area thirty-six. The three corner triangles have areas six, nine and six, which is twenty-one. Take them away, and the triangle's area is fifteen square units.

points: Midpoint = mean of x's, mean of y's
Same y: horizontal. Same x: vertical
Height is measured from the base
scenes.say: Quick recap. The midpoint is the mean of the x values and the mean of the y values. For a missing end, take the same step again. Read lengths by subtracting coordinates carefully across zero. And for slanted shapes, box it and chop the corners. Now try the practice questions!
